name: NJ-12
label: Safe D

key_factors: Huge Democratic fundraising and outside-spending advantage
Open seat removes incumbency but not the partisan baseline
model.rationale: NJ-12's D+13 lean, the Democrat's roughly 20-to-1 fundraising edge plus $1.9 million in outside support, and markets pricing a Democratic win near 96% all point to a comfortable hold despite the open seat. The Republican nominee has raised under $80,000, leaving no evidence of a competitive race.
model.watch: A late surge of Republican outside spending or an unusually favorable national environment could narrow the margin, though not plausibly enough to threaten the seat.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Bonnie Watson Coleman (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Bonnie Watson Coleman's retirement leaves this central New Jersey seat open, but the district's D+13 partisan lean keeps it firmly in Democratic column territory. Adam Hamawy has raised about $1.5 million and benefits from nearly $2 million in outside support, while Republican Gregg Mele has raised under $80,000 with almost no cash on hand and no outside help.

Prediction markets give Democrats roughly a 96% chance of holding the seat, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive. With no public polling available, the forecast rests on fundamentals, which consistently point to a safe Democratic hold in the low-twenties margin range.
